decisions.quote: We observed that low-wealth subjects given fewer chances to win in repeated “Wheel of Fortune” type word puzzle games, performed worse on the Dots-Mixed attention task (M = 41.56, SD = 16.79) than high-wealth individuals (M = 42.82, SD = 15.87), however, this result was not statistically significant (F(1,666) = .99, p=.319). This result did not replicate the findings from Study 1 of Shah et al. (2012), but the means were not in the opposite direction of their results as seen in Camerer et al. (2018).
decisions.reason: Under Codebook Step 2 (replication chains), Camerer et al. (2018) (10.1038/s41562-018-0399-z, paired with blind target 2) is the closest target in the chain, as O'Donnell et al. (2021) replicated the Camerer et al. (2018) replication of Study 1 from Shah, Mullainathan, and Shafir (2012) using Camerer et al.'s materials and sample size baseline. However, the primary report explicitly judges replication failure only against Shah et al. (2012) and merely contrasts the direction of the non-significant sample means with Camerer et al. (2018) without stating Camerer et al.'s inferential result or a replication verdict on Camerer et al. (2018) itself. While the project spreadsheet (line 1052) lists non-significant effects for both Camerer et al. (2018) (F(1,617) = 0.1389, r = 0.015) and the replication (F(1,666) = .99, r = 0.039) (which would suggest null-to-null agreement), the main text (line 17) evaluates all 20 studies against positive scarcity predictions and counts only references 4 and 16-18 as successful replications. Because the source does not unambiguously settle the original-specific outcome for Camerer et al. (2018), the outcome is undeterminable.
